design_summary: In-game and editor tooling that lets humans and AIs build, debug, test, and diagram the game from inside a running Godot session. Spans a unified debug overlay/drawer, a JSON-driven level editor, an RCON console and test runner, a splay pose authoring system, a collaborative whiteboard, plus a webcam motion-capture bridge for procedural-animation tuning. Nearly all surfaces route through the RCON server on port 9999 so tests and scripts can drive them headlessly.

standalone_designs.title: Motion Capture Bridge
standalone_designs.summary: A Python (MediaPipe) to Godot TCP bridge that streams webcam skeleton data into the running game to drive a quadruped's skeleton in real time for animation tuning. Includes a 2.5D projection pipeline, pinning, calibration poses, and a config slider panel. Cross-cutting animation tooling, not tied to a single feature epic.

standalone_designs.title: Config Panel Redesign
standalone_designs.summary: Restructures the debug drawer Config tab into 10 cross-linked sub-sections with class-level defaults, per-entity stat breakdowns, and modifier calculation chains. Establishes the principle that every physics body gets its own config stack and JSON default file.

epics.title: Debug Overlay & Developer Tools
epics.summary: Replaces ad-hoc debug rendering with a unified DebugOverlay singleton: a 2-level aspect tree, an observer model (human/test/script), entity filtering, and a slide-out drawer for in-game configuration. All debug visuals and logs route through one API, drivable from RCON and test JSON. The drawer grew into a multi-section dockable panel hosting debug aspects, the test runner, config, level editor, and blueprints.

epics.title: Splay Pose System
epics.summary: A system for placing creatures in reusable, world-tethered poses. Splay poses are JSON definitions of connection points and cast directions; instances place posed creatures in levels, auto-creating tethers and IK-overriding the skeleton. Includes asleep behavior, dramatic breakaway, multi-creature splays, instance/pose editor modes, a pose library, and RCON commands.
